versions.name: RXV2-0.9.347-rename-returns
versions.notes: After renaming a receiver (or finishing first-run setup) in the app, you're taken straight back to the model list, where it reappears under its new name — no more force-quitting to reconnect.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.346-short-caption
versions.notes: Shorter, calmer graph caption: 'Each line auto-scaled to its own range (min-max in the key).' The tutorial sentence moved out of the way.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.345-instant-check
versions.notes: The manual Check-for-Update page is now as instant as the automatic prompt: inside the app it reads the release list with the PHONE's internet (like the front-page banner always did) instead of asking the receiver to fetch web pages over its own WiFi — which was slow at best and impossible with the transmitter on.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.344-event-afterlife
versions.notes: Chasing the Bluetooth-dead-after-landing bug: the event log now SURVIVES reboots (persisted to flash at safe moments, previous boot readable afterwards and captured by session saves), and a watchdog keeps re-trying the post-landing Bluetooth revival every 30 s instead of leaving you to reboot.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.343-telem-watchdog
versions.notes: Chasing the field telemetry dropout: the event log now records exactly WHEN flight-controller telemetry stops and when it resumes (with durations), and the battery-cell-count query stops pestering flight controllers that never answer it.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.342-proven-tune-nudge
versions.notes: The receiver now notices when a tune has PROVEN itself: after Rotorflight edits followed by six or more flights with no further changes, the app's front page gently suggests backing the tune up to the phone — once per tune, dismissable. Works across battery cycles and counts transmitter edits too.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.341-fewer-twitches
versions.notes: The little swashplate twitch during bank changes and saves is the flight controller pausing to write its memory (the official Configurator does it too) — harmless, now explained in the help. The app also skips unnecessary bank changes during backup and restore, so it happens less.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.340-backup-help
versions.notes: Help screens now spell out that backing up to the phone captures ALL the Black box data (every saved flight and the event log) as well as every bank's Rotorflight settings — the phone becomes a complete backup of the model.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.339-one-backup-system
versions.notes: One backup system: the Rotorflight page now carries 'Back up settings to phone' and 'Restore settings from phone' side by side (the phone recording covers every bank, verified on restore). The old receiver-side named-backups page is retired.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.338-maxvel-editable
versions.notes: Rates page: Max Vel is now editable (it shares one stored value with Rate — editing either keeps the other in step, matching the official Configurator).

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.337-named-verify
versions.notes: Phone-restore polish: each item now gets a second attempt if a radio hiccup interrupts it, and anything that still fails to verify is named ('rates bank 2') instead of counted — so you know exactly what to check.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.336-phone-restore
versions.notes: The confused pilot's parachute: 'Restore settings from phone' on the Rotorflight page writes back EVERY recorded setting — PIDs, advanced PIDs, rates and governor, all four banks — from the app's session recording, even if no backup was ever made. Transmitter must be off; every item is verified by read-back.
